collision_matrix.title: SynCraft: Guiding Large Language Models to Predict Edit Sequences for Molecular Synthesizability Optimization
collision_matrix.overlap: Both address molecular synthesizability optimization through edit sequences.
collision_matrix.differentiation: The survivor adds ontology-grounded diagnosis of why a molecule is non-synthesizable and explicit preservation of pharmacophoric anchors, stereochemistry, and binding interactions.
collision_matrix.risk_rationale: CONTEXT.literature.syncraft.reported gives P2M 28.4% / ResGen 29.1% rescue at similarity>0.6, so edit-sequence rescue overlap is material; however CONTEXT.literature.syncraft does not state ontology-grounded failure explanation or anchor contracts.

collision_matrix.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
collision_matrix.overlap: Both concern AI-agent workflows and evidence sufficiency.
collision_matrix.differentiation: The survivor is a domain-specific ontology-grounded molecular editing pipeline, not an open-ended AI research agent case study.
collision_matrix.risk_rationale: CONTEXT.literature.crux.lesson warns that agents do engineering but fail at evidence sufficiency, which is a caution rather than a direct method collision.

collision_matrix.overlap: They are retrieved structure-paper context; CONTEXT.question mentions binding interactions.

collision_matrix.risk_rationale: No method collision is stated in CONTEXT.literature.structure_papers; they are listed as structure papers.
